sumInsured: As per Policy Schedule (not specified in provided extract)

great.name: Room rent: No limit (base benefit)
great.quote: The eligible Room Rent or Room Category applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is 'No limit', which means that there is no separate restriction on Room Charges incurred towards stay during Hospitalization
great.explanation: No room category capping in the base plan helps avoid proportional deductions tied to room upgrades.

great.name: ICU charges: No limit
great.quote: Intensive Care Unit Charges (ICU Charges): The eligible ICU Charges applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is 'No limit', which means that there is no separate restriction on ICU Charges incurred towards stay in ICU during Hospitalization.
great.explanation: No separate ICU cap; ICU expenses are covered up to Sum Insured and other available buffers.

great.name: Restore/Reinstatement: Unlimited Automatic Recharge (same illness allowed)
great.quote: automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year... Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness as well as different Illnesses.
great.explanation: Strong restore benefit: after base SI + bonuses (and plus benefit if opted) are exhausted, the base SI can be reinstated unlimited times in the same policy year, even for the same illness.

great.name: NCB/Renewal Bonus: 50% per year and does not reduce on claim
great.quote: enhance the Sum Insured by 50% flat... (vi) In the event of a Claim there is no impact on the accrual of Cumulative Bonus.
great.explanation: Your Sum Insured can grow by 50% each claim-free renewal, and the accrual is not impacted by claims (unusually customer-friendly versus typical NCB reset structures).

great.name: Built-in additional Sum Insured buffer: Unlimited Automatic Recharge (activates after base SI exhausted)
great.quote: The Recharge shall be utilized only after the base Sum Insured, applicable Cumulative Bonus , Cumulative Bonus Super (if applicable) and Plus Benefit (if applicable) have been completely exhausted in that Policy Year.
great.explanation: Additional coverage becomes available after exhausting base SI and accrued/add-on buffers, giving a large backstop for multiple/large claims in a year.

great.name: Specific illness (Named Ailment) waiting period: 24 months
great.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/ treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
great.explanation: Named ailments are covered after 24 months continuous coverage, which is standard-to-good and per your rules qualifies as GOOD, but it is still a strong clarity point; the policy explicitly sets 24 months.

good.name: PED waiting period: 36 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months continuous coverage (3 years), which is within the acceptable 24–48 month band.

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Standard 30-day initial waiting for non-accident illness.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization cover: 60 days
good.quote: For a period of 60 days immediately prior to the Insured Person's date of admission to the Hospital
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for 60 days before hospitalization (for the same condition), which is standard.

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover: 180 days
good.quote: For a period of 180 days immediately after the Insured Person's date of discharge from the hospital
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for 180 days after discharge (for the same condition), which is standard/good.

good.name: Domiciliary hospitalization: Covered (with conditions)
good.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person... for the Medical Expenses incurred towards Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.explanation: Home hospitalization is covered (reimbursement) subject to conditions like >3 days and exclusions of certain listed illnesses.

good.name: Air ambulance: Available as optional benefit
good.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person up to the amount as specified in Policy Schedule , for the Reasonable and Customary Charges necessarily incurred on availing Air Ambulance services
good.explanation: Air ambulance is offered as an add-on/optional benefit (limit as per schedule).

bad.name: Consumables not covered by default (unless Claim Shield optional benefit is taken) — out-of-pocket risk
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – I to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.reference: Clause 4.2(1) + Annexure I (List of Expenses Generally Excluded)
bad.explanation: Annexure I lists many consumables/non-medical items (e.g., gloves, masks, nebulisation kit, etc.) as excluded by default. This can increase out-of-pocket costs unless you opt for the 'Claim Shield' optional benefit that pays List-I items.

bad.name: Mandatory disease/procedure sub-limits possible if specified in Policy Schedule (policy explicitly allows them)
bad.quote: For diseases or conditions or procedure that have a specified sub-limit then all related expenses shall be covered up to the sub-limit specified for that disease or condition or procedure.
bad.explanation: If your policy schedule includes any disease-wise sub-limits (e.g., cataract cap), then claims for those conditions are capped at that sub-limit. This is a red-flag risk area to verify in your specific policy schedule.

unclear.name: Co-pay (base policy): not explicitly stated unless optional covers are chosen
unclear.quote: The Co-payment proportion ( If opted ) shall be borne by the Insured Person on each Claim
unclear.reference: General Conditions Applicable To All The Benefits And Optional Benefits, point 4 + Optional Benefit 3.2.7
unclear.explanation: The wording explains co-pay only as an optional feature (and additional co-pays under optional covers like Smart Select/True Connect). It does not clearly state whether the default base plan has 0% co-pay. Confirm from your policy schedule.

unclear.name: NCB / Renewal Bonus: maximum accumulation beyond 100% unclear if any other bonus/plus can apply simultaneously (schedule-dependent)
unclear.quote: the accrued Cumulative Bonus, shall not exceed 100% of the Sum Insured
unclear.explanation: Cumulative Bonus is capped at 100% of SI, but the policy also has optional 'Cumulative Bonus Super' and 'Plus Benefit'. Your effective total buffer depends on which optional benefits you have in the schedule.

unclear.name: Sum Insured and selected optional benefits are schedule-dependent (not provided)
unclear.quote: Sum Insured means the amount specified in the Policy Schedule
unclear.explanation: Key values (Sum Insured, and whether add-ons like Plus Benefit/Claim Shield/Cumulative Bonus Super/Unlimited Care are opted) are not in the provided extract; they must be checked in your policy schedule.
